sections.html:
Spokane is the seat of Spokane County, on the Spokane River in eastern Washington, less than 20 miles from the Idaho line. It had 230,783 residents in July 2025, second in the state after Seattle. Fewer city households own their homes than in the county as a whole, so a good share of Spokane houses are rentals when they sell. The 2020 to 2024 numbers for the city and the county:

Housing measureSpokane citySpokane County
Median owner-occupied home value$363,500$410,700
Owner-occupied housing rate58.8%64.5%
Median gross rent$1,215$1,283
Households97,446218,395

Which school district a house sits in changes its levy. Spokane Public Schools covers most of the city, while the Mead district serves north county outside the city limits. Look up the address on the county parcel record before you quote anyone a tax figure.

sections.h2: Who bills property tax for a Spokane house?
sections.html:
The city does not send a property tax bill. The Spokane County Treasurer bills and collects, and the Spokane County Assessor sets the value. The City of Spokane is one of roughly 56 taxing districts in the county that hand their budgets to the Assessor each November.

The city's share goes mainly into the General Fund for police, fire, streets, parks and the library. Its proposed 2025 to 2026 budget assumed the 1% increase allowed on regular levies, and it carries a streets levy and a public safety personnel levy fund as dedicated revenue. The rest of a Spokane bill comes from the county, the school district, the state school levy and any special district over the parcel.

Water, sewer and trash service are paid by fees, not property tax. Before you close, ask the city utility billing office whether the address has an unpaid utility balance.

  • Treasurer: Spokane County Courthouse, 1116 W. Broadway Ave., 509-477-4713, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
  • Assessor: 509-477-3698.
  • Payments by mail: Spokane County Treasurer, P.O. Box 199, Spokane, WA 99210.

Tax is due in two halves, April 30 and October 31. A bill under $50 is due in full on April 30. When a date lands on a weekend or county holiday, payment is accepted the next business day. The next date after this fall's second half is April 30, 2027.

One statement a year arrives with two coupons. If yours is missing by March 31, call 509-477-4713 or find it on SCOUT, the county's online lookup. If a mortgage company pays from escrow, confirm with your lender, because the county does not bill lenders directly or keep their information.

The courthouse has two drop boxes, and they take checks only. In the weeks before each due date the Treasurer also collects in person at Spokane Valley City Hall and the North Spokane Library, on two Fridays and two Tuesdays. Mail counts by federal postmark, and postal changes have delayed postmarks lately, so send it early.

Interest starts May 1 for a missed first half and November 1 for a missed second half, and it runs on the full year's amount. A home with four or fewer units pays 0.75% per month and no penalty. Other property pays 1% per month, plus a 3% penalty on June 1 and 8% on December 1.

State law lets the Treasurer set up payment agreements and accept partial payments on current and past-due taxes, with money going to the oldest year first (RCW 84.56.020). A hardship waiver after the death of a spouse, parent or stepparent needs notice within 60 days of the due date (RCW 84.56.025). Interest cannot be waived when the statement went to an address supplied by the taxpayer or the taxpayer's agent, a closing agent for example.

A returned payment carries a $30 fee, plus whatever interest, penalty and costs apply.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Spokane assessment?
sections.html:
A city of Spokane assessment is appealed to the Spokane County Board of Equalization, not City Hall. File the petition form by July 1 of the assessment year, or within 30 days after the Change of Value Notice was mailed, whichever is later. There is no fee. A phone call or letter will not stand in for the form.

The board looks only at market value, and the assessor's number is presumed right unless your evidence is clear, cogent and convincing (RCW 84.40.0301). Build your case around these points:

  • Tax amount, percentage increase, other properties' values and personal hardship cannot be considered.
  • Comparable sales close to January 1 of the assessment year make the strongest case.
  • Extra evidence is due seven business days before the hearing.
  • Notice of the hearing comes 15 business days ahead.

Call the Assessor first at 509-477-3698, since many disagreements end in a stipulated value. If you lose, you have 30 calendar days to go to the State Board of Tax Appeals. The county revalues every parcel each year and inspects each one at least once in six years.

Seniors and people retired because of disability can apply for a property tax exemption through the Spokane County Assessor at 509-477-3698. Senate Bill 6162, signed after the 2026 session, changes the income limits starting in 2027, so ask for the limits that apply to you instead of trusting older numbers.

Every tax statement must carry a notice about the exemption and the state deferral program (RCW 84.56.020). An owner who is income-qualified, lives in the home and faces a tax foreclosure action can have interest and penalties waived about three years after delinquency, once per property.

The Board of Equalization may also reconvene past the usual deadline for a buyer who bought after July 1 and before December 31 of the assessment year for less than 90% of the assessed value.

sections.h2: What should you do about back taxes when selling in Spokane?
sections.html:
Ask the Treasurer for a payoff covering every year owed, hand it to the closing agent, and confirm the agent has your correct parcel number and mailing address. Remember that interest stays in place if the county's statement was mailed to an address the closing agent supplied.

Real estate excise tax is payable to the county treasurer on the date of sale, and the seller usually pays it. For sales from January 1, 2027, a house at the city's $363,500 median value falls entirely in the 1.1% state bracket, before any local rate is added.

Waiting is risky. Once tax sits unpaid three years after delinquency, the treasurer must start foreclosure by certificate of delinquency (RCW 84.64.050).

sections.h2: Closing checklist for a Spokane seller
sections.html:
A tidy tax file makes a sale move faster. Start a few weeks before you list and work down this list:

  • Pull the parcel record on SCOUT and write down the parcel number, the school district and what each half shows as paid.
  • Call the Treasurer at 509-477-4713 and ask for a written payoff if anything is open from a prior year.
  • Ask the city utility billing office about any water, sewer or trash balance on the address.
  • Tell the Assessor at 509-477-3698 if a senior or disability exemption or a deferral is attached, so the closing agent knows to plan for it.
  • Give the closing agent a mailing address you actually check, because late-notice mail goes to whatever address is on file.

A buyer paying cash can often close on a short timeline, and a cash purchase skips the lender's own tax review. You still need the payoff, since the Treasurer collects unpaid tax, interest and penalties from the proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to in Spokane?
faqs.a: The Spokane County Treasurer, at 1116 W. Broadway Ave. or P.O. Box 199, Spokane, WA 99210, or online. Call 509-477-4713. The city itself does not collect the tax.

faqs.q: When is Spokane property tax due?
faqs.a: April 30 and October 31, with bills under $50 due in full April 30. The next date is April 30, 2027, or the following business day if that falls on a weekend.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Spokane property value?
faqs.a: File a petition with the Spokane County Board of Equalization by July 1 of the assessment year or within 30 days of the Change of Value Notice, whichever is later. It is free, and you need market value evidence such as comparable sales.

faqs.q: What interest applies to late Spokane property tax?
faqs.a: For a home with four or fewer units, 0.75% a month with no penalty. Other property pays 1% a month plus 3% on June 1 and 8% on December 1, all on the whole year's tax.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Spokane house that owes back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax, interest and penalties are paid from the proceeds at closing. Call the Spokane County Treasurer for a payoff and give the closing agent your correct parcel number and mailing address.
